answer: An agent economy can require each identity to climb a chain of interdependent jobs: each later job starts only from the verified output of an earlier one, assigned at unpredictable times. Like a summit route where each camp depends on the last ascent, a newcomer cannot skip ahead. A cipher key for one step unlocks only the next step for that identity, so copying it duplicates no progress. A saffron grower must prove harvest, then delivery, then payment, in order. An attacker making a thousand fakes must complete a thousand chains, each costing time and work, while an honest agent pays once.
